question: What is the process to upgrade an unmanaged package that is currently installed in production?
optionA: Install the new version to a Developer org then deploy to production.
optionB: Uninstall the current version and install the new version.
optionC: Click the update link on the Installed Packages page.
optionD: Use the Install Wizard to install the upgrade to production.
explanation:
Unmanaged packages CANNOT be upgraded. Once installed, the only way to get a newer version of an unmanaged package into an org is to uninstall the existing version and install the new version. There is no 'update' link for unmanaged packages on the Installed Packages page — that is a feature of managed packages only. Reference: Salesforce Help — 'Unmanaged packages aren't upgradeable.'
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg1_dev.meta/pkg1_dev/packaging_developing_unmanaged.htm

question: An app builder would like to streamline the user experience by reflecting summarized calculations of specific fields on various objects. Which field types could be used in roll-up summary fields to accomplish this? Choose 3 answers
optionC: Date
explanation:
Roll-up summary fields aggregate values from child records in a master-detail relationship. The field being summarized must be numeric or date-based. Currency, Number, and Percent fields support SUM, MIN, MAX (and COUNT). Date fields support MIN and MAX. Checkbox and Time fields cannot be used as the aggregated field in a roll-up summary. (COUNT works on any related record regardless of field type, but the question is about which field types can be summarized.)
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) increased its Salesforce development efforts so that it now has multiple custom development efforts happening in parallel. CK's developers and admins perform the customizations and have complained that working in one sandbox has led to many problems. They requested a solution in which they can work in at least 20 different sandboxes at once, that all start with the same base configuration and data. What should an app builder use to solve the problem?
optionC: Partial copy sandboxes
explanation:
Sandbox cloning is the feature written for this scenario, and Salesforce describes it in almost the stem's words: 'You can create a sandbox by cloning an existing sandbox rather than using your production org as your source. Save time by customizing a sandbox with a set of data and metadata and then replicating it. Sandbox cloning simplifies having multiple concurrent streams of work in your application life cycle... Your colleagues can easily clone individual sandboxes instead of sharing one sandbox and avoid stepping on each other's toes.' That covers all three requirements — parallel streams of work, escaping a single shared sandbox, and every environment starting from one common baseline, since 'when you clone a sandbox, its data and metadata are copied to the new sandbox.'
The sandbox *types* cannot deliver the same thing, because each one copies from production rather than from a prepared baseline. A Partial Copy sandbox 'includes a copy of your production org's configuration (metadata) and a sample of your production org's data as defined by a sandbox template' — so twenty of them would each be a fresh slice of production, not twenty copies of the team's agreed starting configuration. Partial Copy is also a paid add-on for Enterprise, Unlimited and Performance editions rather than something available in twenties; Developer sandboxes are the type that ships in quantity, and they carry metadata only, which is precisely why cloning is what gets a common set of *data* into them.
One practical note the documentation adds: 'A cloned sandbox uses the same license type as its source org', so cloning organises the environments rather than conjuring extra licences. Refreshes (A) only re-copy an existing sandbox from its source, and Full sandboxes (B) are the least plausible at this count.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.data_sandbox_cloning_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.create_test_instance.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved C->D. The Sandbox Cloning article matches this stem clause by clause — 'multiple concurrent streams of work', colleagues cloning 'instead of sharing one sandbox', and 'customizing a sandbox with a set of data and metadata and then replicating it' for the common baseline. The old key rested on Partial Copy being licensed in larger quantities than Full, which is true but does not reach twenty, and misses the real defect: every sandbox type copies from production, so no quantity of fresh Partial Copies gives twenty environments sharing one prepared configuration. Cloning is also what puts data into Developer sandboxes, which are the type that actually ships in quantity and otherwise carry metadata only.

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) wants to set up a custom child object to track gift cards issued to a customer. A key requirement is to track the total number of gift cards opened and gift cards issued on an Account. CK wants to permanently ensure the gift cards are unable to be moved across any other Account once it is created. On the gift card object, what type of field should be created to support this requirement?
optionC: Formula
explanation:
Master-detail relationships (with 'Allow reparenting' unchecked, which is the default) prevent child records from being moved to another parent — satisfying the 'unable to be moved across any other Account' requirement. They also enable roll-up summary fields on the parent (Account) to count gift cards. A lookup relationship would allow the parent to be changed and does not support roll-up summaries.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: At Universal Containers, all US Sales Reps should be able to view the US Team dashboard, however, only the US Sales Directors should be able to see the data in the component and view its source report. How can an app builder ensure the proper access is granted?
optionA: Make the US Sales Director the running user and share the dashboard folder with the role US Sales Rep.
optionB: Make the dashboard dynamic and give US Sales Reps the View My Team's Dashboard permission.
optionC: Share the dashboard folder with roles and subordinates of the US Sales Director and share the report folder with the role of US Sales Director.
optionD: Share the dashboard with the public group US Sales Reps and share the dashboard source reports folder with the US Sales Director profile.
explanation:
Folder access is what separates the two audiences here. Sharing the dashboard folder with Roles and Subordinates of the US Sales Director gives every rep beneath that role the ability to open the dashboard, while sharing the source report's folder only with the US Sales Director role means only directors can open the underlying report — which is the drill-down half of the requirement.
One mechanism worth being precise about, because it is easy to state backwards. Restricting the report folder does not hide the numbers rendered in the dashboard. A dashboard runs as its running user, and Salesforce's own worked example of Viewer access describes a sales rep who checks his standing on a dashboard and 'must view the data in the underlying reports' yet needs nothing more than 'Viewer access to the folder that contains the Master Sales dashboard'. So reps who can open this dashboard will see the component values; what they will not be able to do is open or drill into the source report.
Read the requirement's 'see the data in the component' as being about reaching the report behind it rather than about the summary figures on the dashboard face. The other options fail more plainly: making the director the running user (A) changes whose data is shown without restricting report access, dynamic dashboards (B) show each viewer their own data and cannot be the answer to a shared team dashboard, and sharing a dashboard directly with a public group (D) is not how dashboard access is granted — folders are.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.analytics_folder_viewer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.analytics_folder_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands, but the old explanation was wrong on mechanism and has been corrected. It claimed that 'by restricting the report folder, only directors can see the underlying numbers'. The Viewer Access article contradicts that with a worked example: a sales rep who refreshes a dashboard and views the data in its underlying reports needs only Viewer access to the dashboard's folder. Dashboard components render as the running user, so report-folder access controls drill-down, not whether the component displays values. That makes the stem's 'see the data in the component' imprecise — flagged rather than silently confirmed, since a learner could otherwise take away a false model of dashboard security. The key is still the best answer because it is the only option that grants reps the dashboard while confining source-report access to directors.

question: Cloud Kicks is redefining its entire business process to convert the Manager Notes field from a long text area field. The goal is to encourage managers to be more concise in their comments and stay at 255 characters or less. There is preexisting information in the Manager Notes field that often is well beyond the character limit. What would happen to any existing information if the app builder tries to convert a preexisting long text area field to text area?
optionA: Preexisting information will truncate to the first 255 characters.
optionB: Preexisting information will remain even if it was over 255 characters.
optionC: Preexisting information will cause an error message to pop up.
optionD: Preexisting information in the field will be completely lost.
explanation:
When converting a Long Text Area to Text (max 255), Salesforce truncates existing values to the first 255 characters. The setup screen will warn that data may be truncated, but the conversion proceeds and excess characters are lost.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which Opportunity standard fields are available to be configured directly? Choose 3 answers
optionC: Lead Source
explanation:
Stage, Lead Source, and Type are standard picklist fields on Opportunity whose values can be edited directly. Forecast Category is derived automatically from the Stage value (configured via the Stage picklist's Forecast Category mapping, not directly). Probability is also automatically tied to Stage.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A new field has been added to the Applicant object that is part of an unmanaged package. A recruiter ran the Position with or without Applicants report and noticed that the new field was missing as an option to add as a column. How should an app builder troubleshoot this issue?
optionA: Adjust the field-level security to include in the report type.
optionB: Check Allow Reports for the Position and Applicant objects.
optionC: Add the field to the custom report type field layout.
optionD: Update the profile with the Manage Public Reports permission.
explanation:
Custom report types do not automatically include new fields added to an object. The app builder must edit the custom report type and explicitly add the new field to its field layout to make it available as a column in reports built from that report type.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000384387&language=en_US&type=1
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_manage_report_type.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder received a request to extend record access beyond the organization-wide defaults configured. Which two features satisfy this requirement? Choose 2 answers
optionC: Permission Set Groups
explanation:
Sharing rules and manual sharing are the standard mechanisms for opening up record access beyond OWD. Sharing rules grant access to groups of users based on ownership or criteria. Manual sharing grants access to specific users or groups on individual records. Public groups are containers used inside sharing rules — they don't grant access on their own. Permission set groups bundle object/field/system permissions, not record-level access.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.managing_the_sharing_model.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers manages leads in a Lead qualification queue where sales reps can accept ownership of the Lead. Campaign members are required to have a sales owner. What validation rule should an app builder configure?
optionC: AND(ISNEW(), ISBLANK(Owner:User.Id))
explanation:
Campaign members must have a sales (user) owner. The validation rule should fire whenever the Lead is owned by a queue (i.e., Owner:Queue.Id is not blank). NOT(ISBLANK(Owner:Queue.Id)) returns TRUE when the owner is a queue, blocking the save and forcing a sales rep to take ownership. Option C only blocks new records, not existing ones being edited while still owned by the queue.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder wants to create a report to compare the number of support cases in each status (New, In-Progress, or Closed) and by priority (Critical, High, Medium, or Low). What solution should be used for the report?
optionC: Custom Report Type
explanation:
Grouping rows by Status and columns by Priority (a matrix report / summary with two groupings) produces exactly the comparison the requirement describes. Bucket columns categorize values into custom groups, filters narrow data shown, and custom report types define which objects/fields are reportable — none of these compare counts across two dimensions on their own.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.reports_builder_fields_groupings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Sales reps want the ability to see who can view their account records and how the people have access. Which button should the app builder add to the Account page layout to enable this?
optionC: Sharing Hierarchy
explanation:
The Sharing button on a record opens the Sharing Detail page, which lists every user with access and the reason for that access (owner, role hierarchy, sharing rule, manual share, team, etc.). Sharing Hierarchy shows role-hierarchy access only and is not an addable button on the page layout in the same way.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.granting_access_to_records_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder is tasked with adding key performance indicators on Account pages. They want to see a summary of the number of open Opportunities and the number of won Opportunities for each Account. Where should the app builder go to build these new rollups?
optionC: Lightning Object Creator
explanation:
Roll-up summary fields are created on the parent (master) object. Account is the master in the Account–Opportunity relationship, so the roll-up summary fields counting open and won Opportunities are created on the Account object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: When an Opportunity Close Date is pushed more than 30 days, manager approval is required. An approval process is in place but reps frequently forget to submit for approval to run the process. How can an app builder ensure that these opportunities are submitted into the approval process?
optionA: Change the entry criteria on the approval process to criteria are met and lock the record on initial submission.
optionB: Use a validation rule and an email alert to the manager requesting approval.
optionC: Submit the record for approval from an automated process.
optionD: Give the manager the API Enabled permission to permit approval responses by email.
explanation:
A record-triggered flow (or Process Builder) can call the 'Submit for Approval' action automatically when the Close Date is pushed by more than 30 days, removing the need for the rep to remember. Approval process entry criteria alone do not submit a record — submission is always an explicit action.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to deliver purchased containers to remote construction addresses. In these cases, the customers will supply UC with the coordinates to the location. What type of field should the app builder use to capture this information?
optionC: Text
explanation:
A geolocation field stores latitude and longitude as a compound field and supports distance calculations in formulas, reports, and SOQL — the appropriate native field type for capturing coordinates.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_types.htm&type=5&language=en_US

question: DreamHouse Realty (DR) asks for some improvements in case management. They want to enforce process compliance so that cases are unable to be reverted to an earlier case status, and to ensure that certain fields are required when specific case criteria are met. Which solution should an app builder implement to meet these requirements?
optionA: Configure validation rules with help text.
optionB: Create dependent picklist fields and set them as required.
optionC: Use an approval process to check field criteria are met.
optionD: Make the fields required on the page layout.
explanation:
Validation rules can compare PRIORVALUE(Status) to the new Status to block backward moves, and can conditionally require fields based on other field values (something page-layout 'Required' cannot do, since that makes the field required unconditionally). Both compliance requirements are met with validation rules.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_field_validation.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_priorvalue.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: To increase adoption, Universal Containers is proposing changes to its Salesforce data model to allow easier visibility for sales reps into key metrics. The proposal has three custom objects related to the Account object, one with a master-detail, and two that are not. Each of these objects has 15 fields they would like to summarize on the Account object. What are two considerations for this proposal? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Roll-up summaries allow MAX, MIN, SUM, COUNT, and AVG.
optionB: An object can have 20 object references.
optionC: An object can have 25 roll-up summaries.
optionD: Roll-up summaries are limited to master-detail relationships.
explanation:
Two true considerations: (D) roll-up summary fields can only be created across master-detail relationships, so the two lookup-related objects cannot be summarized natively; (C) the standard limit is 25 roll-up summary fields per object (raisable to 40 by Salesforce). Option A is wrong because roll-up summaries support COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX — not AVG.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has created a picklist field called Status on three separate custom objects. UC has a requirement to share the list of values for this field across each object. Which feature would an app builder use?
optionC: Dynamic Action
explanation:
A Global Picklist Value Set (also called a Global Value Set) is a single, centrally managed list of picklist values that can be reused by picklist fields on multiple objects, ensuring consistency and one-place maintenance.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_global_picklists.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: On the Account Lightning record page, users need to see ten fields and the ability to sort and wrap text on their Related Lists. What Related List type would the app builder select for the Related List Lightning component?
optionC: Related List — Single
explanation:
The Enhanced List (Related Lists — Enhanced) component supports up to 10 columns, in-line text wrapping, and column sorting. Basic List displays only a few fields and lacks sort/wrap features.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customizing_related_lists.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Ursa Major Solar's service department gets requests for several types of services, such as installation, repair, and maintenance. Service managers need to be able to tell when maintenance was last done on an asset to help determine if they are meeting contract agreements, but the last maintenance date can be difficult to determine when there are many work orders related to the asset. They think it would be helpful to have a field auto-populated on the Asset record when a maintenance work order gets closed. What tool should an app builder recommend to help meet this requirement?
optionC: Apex Trigger
explanation:
A record-triggered flow on Work Order can detect when status changes to Closed and the type is Maintenance, then update the related Asset's Last Maintenance Date field. Roll-up summary won't work because Asset–WorkOrder is a lookup, not master-detail. Flow is the declarative tool of choice.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters has two custom objects that are part of a master-detail relationship. What determines the ownership and sharing access of the detail record?
optionA: The default owner is set in the parent object's settings.
optionB: The Owner field on the Detail record.
optionC: The Owner field on the Master record.
optionD: The owner is set independently on the detail object's settings.
explanation:
In a master-detail relationship, the detail record does not have its own Owner field. Ownership and sharing of the detail record are inherited from the master (parent) record's owner.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Director of Marketing at Northern Trail Outfitters wants the app builder to create a formula field that tracks how many days have elapsed since a contact was sent a marketing communication. The director is only interested in whole units. Which function should be used to return a date for calculating the difference?
optionC: DATEVALUE()
explanation:
TODAY() returns the current date as a Date value. Subtracting one Date from another yields a whole number of days, which is what the director wants. NOW() returns Date/Time and would produce fractional results.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.formula_using_date_datetime.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is expecting impacts to operations due to increased demand. The executive team will be reaching out to current customers and want to see the number of open cases for the account and parent account. Which tool could an app builder use to display the number of open cases on the Account page?
optionC: Approval Process
explanation:
Account-to-Case is a standard LOOKUP relationship, not master-detail, so a native roll-up summary field cannot be created to count cases — this is a common misconception. A record-triggered flow (or scheduled flow) that counts related open Cases and writes the total to a number field on the Account is the correct no-/low-code tool. Workflow and approval processes cannot aggregate child records.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to delete data in several fields for 5,000 lead records. UC exports the selected record IDs and fields that need to have data deleted in a CSV file. Which two steps should an app builder suggest to meet these requirements? Choose 2 answers
optionB: Use Import Wizard to update Leads using the CSV file.
optionC: Select Insert Null Values in settings.
optionD: Use Data Loader to update Leads using the CSV file.
explanation:
Data Loader has an 'Insert Null Values' setting that, when enabled, lets blank cells in the CSV overwrite existing field values with null — clearing the data. The Data Import Wizard ignores blank values, so it cannot be used to clear fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_import_general_update_blank_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) tracks the support level of its customers on the Account record page. CK wants to show a text notification on a Case record page when the related Account is a platinum-level customer. How could an app builder meet this requirement?
optionA: Add a Rich Text component to the Case Lightning page and set the component visibility to show when the Account Support Level is Platinum.
optionB: Create a text-only Visualforce page, drag the Visualforce component into the Case page layout, and set its visibility to show when the Account Support Level is Platinum.
optionC: Create a text-only Visualforce page, clone the Case page layout, drag the Visualforce component into the page, and assign the layout to platinum cases.
optionD: Clone the Case Lightning page, add a Rich Text area to the new page, and assign this page to platinum accounts.
explanation:
In Lightning App Builder, a Rich Text component supports component visibility filters that can reference fields on the related parent (Account.Support_Level__c). This is the simplest declarative solution and avoids cloning pages or writing Visualforce.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks (CK) keeps track of its shoe inventory in Salesforce. When an order's status is changed to Activated, the inventory for the ordered shoe is reduced. At that point, a SOAP web service on the CK website must be called so that the website is updated to display the correct inventory amount for the shoe. What should an app builder use to communicate to the CK web service when a shoe's inventory has changed?
optionC: Process Builder
explanation:
The requirement is to reach an external SOAP endpoint when inventory changes, and the choice comes down to which automation can act after the record is saved and is still supported.
A before-save record-triggered flow is ruled out by design: before-save flows can only set field values on the record that triggered them, and cannot perform actions, so they cannot call anything outward. That leaves the after-save flow, which can invoke an action — including an outbound message, or Apex that calls the service — once the inventory change is committed.
Be careful with the reason for rejecting the older tools, because it is about support rather than capability. Outbound messaging genuinely does call a SOAP endpoint: Salesforce documents an outbound message as one that 'sends a message to a designated endpoint', and outbound message actions are available to flows, workflow rules, approval processes and entitlement processes alike. So a workflow rule could technically have done this. What disqualifies options C and D is that Workflow Rules and Process Builder reached end of support on 31 December 2025; existing automation continues to run, but neither is the tool to build this with now. Since outbound messaging is available to flows, the after-save flow is also how you would use it today.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_automated_actions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands, but the explanation's dismissal of outbound messaging was wrong and has been corrected. It claimed workflow outbound messages are 'SOAP-style notifications from Salesforce, not arbitrary web service calls', implying they could not satisfy the requirement. Salesforce documents an outbound message as sending 'a message to a designated endpoint' — that is a SOAP web service call, and it is the classic declarative way to make one. So options C and D fail on support status, not on capability: both Process Builder and Workflow Rules hit end of support on 31 Dec 2025. Rewritten so the reader takes away the correct model of outbound messaging, and so the before-save exclusion rests on its documented limitation of updating only the triggering record's fields.

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to change a master-detail relationship on Account to a lookup relationship with a custom object Park. The app builder tries to reconfigure this but is unable to do so. What could be causing this?
optionA: The Account is included in a flow process on the Park object.
optionB: The Park object needs at least one master-detail field for reporting.
optionC: The Account record includes Parks roll-up summary fields.
optionD: The Park records have existing formulas on the Account.
explanation:
Converting a master-detail to a lookup requires removing all roll-up summary fields on the master object that summarize the detail object first, since lookups do not support roll-up summaries. Once the dependent roll-ups are deleted, the conversion can proceed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has created a custom object called Interests which is joined to Accounts by way of a junction object called Account Interest. What is the impact to users attempting to view an Account and the associated Account Interest records if they are without read access to the Interest object?
optionA: Users will be able to view the Account Interest records and will have read-only access to the Interest records.
optionB: Users will be unable to view Account records that have a related Account Interest record.
optionC: Users will be unable to view the Account Interest records or the Interest records.
optionD: Users will be able to view the Account Interest record, but unable to view the field or any information relating back to the Interest record.
explanation:
On a junction object with two master-detail relationships, the user must have at least Read access to BOTH parent objects to see any junction record. Without Read on Interest, the user cannot see any Account Interest junction record, nor any Interest record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.overview_of_custom_object_relationships.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.relationships_manytomany.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An app builder created multiple custom fields, page layouts, and reports in the sandbox and added them to a change set that was deployed to production. The reports were NOT deployed. What should the app builder do?
optionA: Move the reports to the Unfiled Public Reports folder and add them to a new change set.
optionB: Move the reports out of the Unfiled Public Reports folder into a public folder and add them to a new change set.
optionC: Recreate the reports in production. Reports are not supported in change sets.
optionD: Add the reports to an unmanaged package and install the unmanaged package into production.
explanation:
Reports stored in personal folders or in the Unfiled Public Reports folder cannot be added to change sets. The reports must be moved into a shared public report folder before they can be packaged in a change set and deployed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.changesets_about_components.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to test code against a subset of production data that is under 5 GB. Additionally, UC wants to refresh this sandbox every weekend. Which type of sandbox should be used to accomplish this?
optionC: Full Copy
explanation:
Partial Copy sandboxes hold up to 5 GB of data based on a sandbox template and can be refreshed every 5 days, allowing weekly refreshes. Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes don't include production data automatically. Full Copy refreshes every 29 days, so it cannot be refreshed weekly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_environments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.create_test_instance.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a custom object that holds over 100 fields. The app builder wants to break up the fields into separate tabs on the Lightning page. Which Lightning component is most appropriate to fulfill this requirement?
optionC: Field Section
explanation:

question: Cloud Kicks has five years of sales data and would like to track when customers made their first purchase. How should an app builder use a roll-up summary to meet the requirements?
optionA: Create a new roll-up summary field called First Order Date, using type MIN on the Opportunity Close Date with a filter where IsWon = TRUE.
optionB: Create a new date field called First Order Date, create a workflow to set the date, and roll up the value with a filter where IsWon = TRUE.
optionC: Create a new roll-up summary field called First Order Date, using type SUM on Opportunity Close Date.
optionD: Create a new date field called First Order Date, then create a roll-up summary to update the field using type MIN.
explanation:

question: UC has a requirement that an Opportunity should have a field showing the value of its associated Account's Billing State. This value should not change after the Opportunity has been created. What is the recommended solution to configure this automated behavior?
optionC: Workflow rule with Field Update (on create only)
explanation:
The requirement is a value copied once at creation and then frozen, which rules out anything that recalculates. A formula field is therefore wrong on principle rather than on detail: it evaluates every time the record is read, so if the Account's Billing State later changes, the Opportunity's displayed value changes with it — exactly what the requirement forbids. A roll-up summary is doubly inapplicable, since it aggregates child records across a master-detail relationship rather than copying a parent's field.
What satisfies the requirement is automation that writes the value into a plain field on create and never runs again: a workflow rule with a field update, configured to evaluate only when a record is created, copies Account.BillingState into a text field on the Opportunity and leaves it alone thereafter.
One important currency note. Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 December 2025. Existing rules continue to run and can still be edited, so the answer is not wrong, but a solution built today would use a record-triggered flow set to run only on record creation — the same design in the current tool. An Apex trigger (B) would also work and is likewise frozen-on-create, but it is code where clicks suffice.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_about_roll_up_summary_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands, but the item needs a currency flag the old explanation only half gave. Workflow Rules reached end of support on 31 Dec 2025; per the established fact that this is retirement of support rather than removal of capability, an answer keying a workflow rule is still correct, but the explanation now says so explicitly and names the record-triggered flow equivalent instead of mentioning it in passing. Also strengthened the rejection of D, which the old text ignored: a roll-up summary aggregates detail records across a master-detail relationship and cannot copy a parent field at all.

question: The sales team receives a list of approximately 800 leads each morning from the marketing team. The marketing team does not know if any of the leads are currently in the pipeline and sends the entire list each morning. Which tool should be used to import these leads into Salesforce while preventing duplicates from being inserted?

question: An app builder wants to show Groups as the last navigation menu item in the mobile app. However, the app builder is unable to select Groups as one of the items on the drop-down menu. What could cause this?
optionA: Groups is available in the Recent section of the navigation menu.
optionB: Groups is included in the Smart Search Items but unavailable on the navigation menu.
optionC: Groups is unavailable in the selected list for the navigation menu.
optionD: Groups is available in the Chatter section of the navigation menu.
explanation:
Worth reading this item with care, because the documentation does not describe the navigation menu the way the options assume.
In the Mobile Only navigation menu, Groups is itself one of the available items, listed alongside Chatter rather than nested inside it: 'Groups — Appears for organizations that have Chatter enabled. If you don't add this item to the navigation menu, groups and the Groups item are automatically included in the set of Smart Search Items.' So two documented facts bear on the symptom. Groups is available only when Chatter is enabled for the org, and when it is not placed on the menu explicitly it still reaches users through Smart Search Items.
That second behaviour is the most likely explanation for an item that seems to be missing from the picker while remaining reachable in the app: it is being surfaced through Smart Search Items rather than as a menu entry you positioned. It is also why the ordering goal in the stem is hard to achieve — an item delivered through Smart Search Items is not something you can place last in the menu.
The practical checks are therefore whether Chatter is enabled for the org, and whether Groups is already accounted for in the Selected list or via Smart Search Items.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.salesforce_app_customize_nav_menu.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key D left in place but this item looks defective and needs your decision — flagged rather than silently confirmed. The old explanation asserted that Groups 'appears in the Chatter section of the mobile navigation menu rather than as a standalone selectable item'. The Mobile Only Navigation Menu documentation contradicts both halves: it lists Groups as its own available item, and it describes no 'Chatter section' at all — Chatter and Groups are separate entries in the same list. What the documentation does describe is that Groups is available only when Chatter is enabled, and that if you do not add it to the menu, 'groups and the Groups item are automatically included in the set of Smart Search Items' — which is closer to option B than to option D. I did not move the key because option B as worded ('unavailable on the navigation menu') is not documented either, and I could not confirm the exact cause of an item missing from the picker. Recommended repair: reword the options around the documented facts, Chatter-enabled availability and Smart Search Items fallback.

question: The app builder needs to change the data types of new custom fields. The app builder is not able to delete and recreate any of the fields, nor modify any Apex code. Which data type change will require the app builder to perform additional steps in order to retain existing functionality?
optionA: Changing the data type of a field used in an Apex class from Number to Text.
optionB: Changing the data type of a field used in a report from Text to Encrypted.
optionC: Changing the data type of a field used as an external ID from Number to Text.
optionD: Changing the data type of a field used in lead conversion from Number to Text.
explanation:
A is the change that leaves the app builder stuck, but not for the reason people usually give. Salesforce does not let the change through and then break the Apex: it refuses up front. "You can't change the data type of a custom field referenced by other items in Setup such as Visualforce pages, Apex code, processes, or flows." So the additional step is getting the reference out of the Apex first - and the stem forbids exactly that.
The other three are disposed of by documented rules rather than by judgement.
B cannot be done at all, so it is not a matter of extra steps: "an existing custom field can't be converted into an encrypted field nor can an encrypted field be converted into another data type."
C is safe. Changing an external ID field's type only costs you the external ID behaviour when the new type falls outside text, number and email - "choosing a data type other than text, number, or email causes the field to no longer act as an external ID" - and Number to Text stays inside that set.
D is blocked outright as well: "You can't change the data type of any custom field that is mapped for lead conversion."
One thing worth carrying away beyond this question: a field type change is never free even when it is permitted. The conversion runs in the background over every existing record and "in some cases... can take over 24 hours to complete."
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.notes_on_changing_custom_field_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands; the explanation had the mechanism backwards, which the spot-check of the first fifty questions caught. It said a Number to Text change "will cause compile errors in any Apex class or trigger that uses it", implying Salesforce permits the change and the code breaks afterwards. Considerations for Converting the Field Type of a Custom Field says the platform refuses the change while the reference exists: "You can't change the data type of a custom field referenced by other items in Setup such as Visualforce pages, Apex code, processes, or flows." Same answer, opposite sequence of events, and the corrected version explains why the stem's "cannot modify any Apex code" constraint is what makes A the answer. Also tightened B, which the earlier note described as being about "reportability of encrypted data"; the documented rule is that an existing field cannot be converted into an encrypted field at all.

question: An app builder notices several Accounts converted from Leads are missing information they expected to be caught via Account validation rules. What could be the source of this issue?

optionB: Account validation rules fail to validate on records converted from a lead.
optionC: The Lead Settings are allowing users to intentionally bypass validation rules.

question: An app builder wants to deploy a new version of an autolaunched flow to production in an active state so that the new functionality is immediately available to users. What should the app builder take into consideration when planning the deployment?
optionA: Verify there is an Apex test that provides test coverage for the flow.
optionB: Grant user access to the flow.
optionC: Manually activate the flow after deployment.
optionD: Include the Process Builder calling the flow in the deployment.
explanation:
Deploying a flow as active is not the default behaviour, so two things have to be true.
First, the org has to allow it: 'By default, processes and flows that are active in a sandbox or non-production org are deployed to a production org as inactive.' To change that, in Process Automation Settings you select Deploy processes and flows as active and enter a flow test coverage percentage.
Second, the coverage bar has to be met: 'Before you can deploy a process or autolaunched flow as active, make sure you meet flow test coverage requirements. At least one Apex test must cover the flow test coverage percentage of the active processes and autolaunched flows.' That is why verifying Apex test coverage exists for the flow is the planning consideration — and note it applies to autolaunched flows, which is what this stem describes; flows with screens are exempt from flow test coverage requirements.
Be careful with the threshold. The number is whatever percentage the org has configured in Process Automation Settings, not a fixed platform figure, and it is a distinct requirement from the Apex code coverage rule that governs deployments generally. Option C describes exactly the default outcome the requirement is trying to avoid, since manual reactivation is what happens when the active-deployment setting is off.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_deploy_active.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands, but the explanation asserted a number the documentation does not: it claimed deploying an active flow 'requires at least 75% Apex test coverage in the org just like any deployment'. The word 75 does not appear on the Deploy Processes and Flows as Active page at all. What it documents is a configurable flow test coverage percentage, entered in Process Automation Settings, with the requirement that 'at least one Apex test must cover the flow test coverage percentage' — a separate mechanism from the Apex code coverage rule the old text borrowed the figure from. Rewritten to name the real mechanism, to add the prerequisite setting that the old explanation omitted entirely, and to record that screen flows are exempt.

question: Universal Containers (UC) has large data volumes and is nearing data storage limits. The planned solution is to archive historical data to reduce data storage in Salesforce; however, UC would still like to use reports, queries, and lookups on the archived information. Which two options could meet this requirement? Choose 2 answers
optionC: Related Objects
explanation:
Both keyed options keep large volumes of data reportable without consuming standard Salesforce data storage, which is what the requirement needs.
A big object 'stores and manages massive amounts of data on the Salesforce platform', and archiving from other objects into one is a documented use — 'You can archive data from other objects or bring massive datasets from outside systems into a big object'. External objects take the other route: through Salesforce Connect they surface records that remain in the external system, so nothing is copied into Salesforce at all.
One important currency correction on how you get data back out of a big object. Async SOQL is no longer the answer: Salesforce retired it with the Summer '23 release, stating 'You must use the Bulk API or batch Apex to query or report on custom Big Objects'. CRM Analytics still loads big object data, using Bulk API requests. Plan big object reporting around Bulk API or batch Apex rather than Async SOQL.
Also keep the trade-off in view when choosing between them: big objects are built for scale rather than for interactive use, with no standard UI or list views and a deliberately narrow query surface, whereas external objects give live access but depend on the external system's availability. Custom objects (B) would consume the very storage the project is trying to reclaim, and 'Related Objects' (C) is not a Salesforce feature.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.bigobjects.meta/bigobjects/big_object.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000394892&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Key A,D stands, but the explanation cited a retired capability. It justified Big Objects by saying they support 'async SOQL/queries' — Salesforce retired Async SOQL for Big Objects with Summer '23, almost three years before this deck was reviewed, and now directs you to Bulk API or batch Apex to query or report on them. Rewritten to name the current mechanism and to be honest about the trade-off the old text waved at with 'some limitations': big objects have no standard UI or list views and a narrow query surface, so they are archival storage with code-based retrieval rather than a drop-in reporting source.

question: Universal Containers would like to embed a chart of all related Opportunities, by stage, on the Account detail page. Which type of report should the app builder create to add to the Account page layout?

question: Due to the complexity of the Universal Containers sandbox release schedule and requirements, it is advised that change sets are used as often as possible to migrate from one environment to another. Which three common items can an app builder move when using a change set? Choose 3 answers

question: The Service Manager provided the app builder with color code requirements for case age on open cases: New cases populate a green circle, day-old cases populate a yellow circle, three-day-old cases populate a red circle. How should an app builder implement this requirement?
optionC: Custom Button
explanation:
A formula field that returns IMAGE() is the no-code way to put a coloured indicator on a record page, a list view, or a report, and Salesforce documents this exact requirement as a worked sample. "Color Squares for Case Age" displays a 30 x 30 pixel red, yellow, or green image depending on the value of a Case Age field.
Use nested IF() rather than CASE() when the trigger is an age range. CASE() checks an expression for equality against a list of values and returns the matching result, so it switches cleanly on a picklist such as Priority but cannot express "three days old or more". The documented age formula is IF(Case_Age__c > 20, IMAGE(red), IF(Case_Age__c > 10, IMAGE(yellow), IMAGE(green))), with IMAGE() taking a URL, alternate text, and optional height and width.
The other options cost more and deliver less. A quick action (B) and a custom button (C) are things a user clicks, not a value that renders on every row of a list view, and a Lightning web component (D) is custom development for something a formula field already does declaratively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.useful_advanced_formulas_image_links.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_image.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_case.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands; the reasoning was rewritten on a factual point. The original prescribed IMAGE() with CASE() over case age, but CASE is documented as an equality check - "Checks a given expression against a series of values. If the expression is equal to a value, returns the corresponding result" - so it cannot express an age threshold. Salesforce's own sample for precisely this requirement, "Color Squares for Case Age", uses nested IF(). The same article's traffic-light sample confirms the wider claim that image formula fields are meant for list views and reports.

question: Universal Containers wants to display the real-time stock price for each account on the Account record page. How should an app builder implement this request?
optionA: Add a dynamic report to the page layout.
optionC: Install a solution from the AppExchange.
optionD: Build a flow that uses API calls.
explanation:
Displaying a live stock price means calling an external financial API and rendering the result on the Account record page. For an app builder the documented low-effort path is to install a prebuilt solution: on AppExchange you browse or search for a solution, click Get It Now, choose production or sandbox, and install the package, then place the component it ships onto the Account record page in Lightning App Builder. The integration, the credential handling, and the component are all work someone else has already done.
Option D is the closest rival and is no longer impossible. Flow's HTTP Callout connects a flow to an external API without code, and Salesforce's own example is a screen flow making a real-time call to a maps API. But it is a build rather than a buy: it needs a named credential, an external service registration, and familiarity with the provider's API contract, and the flow still has to be surfaced through a screen or a component before anything appears on the record page.
Option A embeds a report, and reports run over Salesforce data, so no report can reach an external price feed. Option B is custom development for a problem the marketplace already solves.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.distribution_installing_packages.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_http_callout.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands, but the explanation was rewritten because it left the strongest distractor unaddressed. Flow HTTP Callout is real and documented - "Use HTTP Callout to connect flows to external APIs without coding, eliminating the need for developers or middleware tools" - so option D is technically feasible today and the item turns on build-versus-buy for an app builder, not on D being impossible. Flagging this as a judgment item rather than a documented one: no Salesforce article says to use AppExchange for a stock price, and a reviewer who weighs the build-versus-buy reading differently could defend D.

question: Universal Containers has several new fields they've requested for the Opportunity Product object. What should an app builder be able to configure using a formula field?
optionA: A hyperlink to the parent Account of the parent Opportunity.
optionB: A Rich Text Area field that uses HTML to bold certain characters.
optionC: A combination of the Opportunity's Name and a Description field.
optionD: A mix of functions and concatenation of 10 Account fields and 10 Opportunity fields.
explanation:
From Opportunity Product (OpportunityLineItem), formulas can traverse to the parent Opportunity and then to the parent Account, and the HYPERLINK() function can build a clickable URL to that grandparent Account record. Formula fields cannot output Rich Text/HTML formatting (B), and option D would likely exceed compiled-formula size limits.
References:

question: The services manager wants to make sure the team enters Case priority consistently. What feature can an app builder use to accomplish this?
optionC: Next Best Action
explanation:
Path is the feature built for this. Salesforce describes it as a way to "boost productivity and help reps gather complete data", and at each step of a path you can highlight key fields and write customised guidance for success. Case is one of the supported objects, so a Case path built on the status picklist can surface Priority as a key field at every step, with guidance telling reps how to set it.
Path guides, it does not enforce. The documented limitation is explicit: you can't use the page layout to require different fields in different steps. If Priority has to be mandatory at a particular step, pair the path with a validation rule written against that path step.
The alternatives solve different problems. A flow (B) automates work behind the scenes rather than coaching the user at the point of entry. Next Best Action (C) surfaces recommended offers and actions, not field-entry guidance. In-App Guidance (D) delivers floating prompts and walkthroughs for feature adoption and is not tied to the fields of the record being edited.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.path_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A stands; the explanation carried a factual error. It said Path key fields can be "required to fill out". Considerations and Guidelines for Creating Paths says the opposite: "You can't use the page layout to require different fields in different steps. However, you can set up validation rules based on a path step." Path highlights and guides; enforcement comes from a validation rule keyed to the step. The rest of the reasoning held - Guide Users with Path lists Cases among the supported objects and frames the feature as helping reps gather complete data, which is what the services manager asked for.

question: An app builder is creating a custom object called Testimonial__c and wants to connect Testimonial__c records with both the submitter's Contact record and Account record. If the Account is deleted, the Testimonial__c should also be deleted. If the Contact is deleted, but the Account remains, the Testimonial__c should remain. How should this be accomplished?
optionA: Make both the Contact and Account fields required on the Testimonial__c object and create lookup relationships from Testimonial__c to Contact and to Account.
optionB: Create a master-detail relationship from Testimonial__c to Account and a lookup relationship from Testimonial__c to Contact.

optionB: Put the SC in the role hierarchy above the technicians whose work orders they review.
optionC: Create a workflow rule that updates records owned by technicians in that region with the SC.
optionD: Change Work Order access on the SC's profile to Modify All.
explanation:

question: The case handling process at Universal Containers includes multiple steps including approvals, notifications, and field updates. To manage and evaluate all of these changes in a single save operation, an app builder wants to use Process Builder and the advanced option to let the process evaluate a record multiple times has been selected. Which two options should the app builder avoid to prevent recursion? Choose 2 answers
optionB: Setting a criteria node to 'No criteria — just execute the actions'
optionC: Invocable processes
explanation:
With the option to let a process evaluate a record up to five times in a single save turned on, the risk is that an action re-triggers the same process. Two of the listed patterns invite that.
A criteria node set to 'No criteria — just execute the actions' has nothing to gate it, so on each re-evaluation it fires again — the classic runaway. And invocable processes introduce mutual triggering, where one process calls another that updates a record and brings the first back into scope.
The two rejected options are the safeguards rather than the hazards. ISCHANGED narrows a criteria node to real transitions of a field, so it stops an action from re-firing when nothing relevant changed, and IF statements are ordinary formula logic used inside criteria.
One important currency note about this whole item. Process Builder reached end of support on 31 December 2025. Existing processes continue to run and can still be edited, so the recursion behaviour described here is still real for orgs that have them, but nothing new should be built in Process Builder. In a record-triggered flow the equivalent discipline is entry conditions plus the option to run the flow only when specified changes are made, which is how you avoid the same loop.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_build_data_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key B,C stands, but this item is built entirely on a tool that reached end of support on 31 Dec 2025, and the explanation now says so. Per the established fact that this is retirement of support rather than removal of capability, the answer remains correct for orgs running existing processes, and the reasoning about ungated criteria nodes and mutually invocable processes is sound. Added the currency flag and named the record-triggered flow equivalent — entry conditions and running only when specified changes are made — so a learner takes away transferable guidance rather than only Process Builder mechanics. Flagged for the user: of the questions reviewed so far, this is the one most tied to a retired tool, and it may be worth rewriting around flows rather than keeping.

question: The Convert button on Leads should NOT appear until the Lead Status picklist is set to Qualified. What should an app builder suggest to meet these requirements?
optionA: Picklist dependency, page layouts, record types
optionB: Custom button, validation rule, record types
optionC: Process Builder field update, quick action, record type
optionD: Page layouts, record types, dynamic forms / dynamic actions
explanation:
Dynamic actions are what make an action's visibility depend on a field value. In Lightning App Builder you assign actions on the Lead record page's Highlights Panel instead of in the page layout editor, then click Add Filter to add visibility rules "based on the record field, device type, or other filters" - here, Lead Status equals Qualified. Below that value the Convert action simply is not rendered, and the standard convert flow is left intact.
Record types and page layouts are supporting cast rather than the mechanism. A layout is fixed for a given record type, so on its own it cannot show or hide Convert as a picklist value changes, and nothing moves a lead between record types when Status changes unless you build automation to do it. They earn their place in the answer only when a genuinely different kind of lead needs a different action set.
Option B works but replaces the standard Convert button with a custom one, which is more to build and more to maintain. Option A confuses picklist dependencies, which control which values are offered in a dependent picklist, with action visibility. Option C is built on Process Builder, which Salesforce stopped supporting on 31 December 2025 and now points to Flow Builder to replace.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_create_dynamic_action.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_components_visibility.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Key D stands, but the explanation led with the part of D that does not work. It opened by proposing separate Unqualified and Qualified record types with their own page layouts and relegated dynamic actions to a parenthesis; a page layout cannot vary with a picklist value, and no record type changes itself when Status changes. Create Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder documents the working mechanism in one line: "To add visibility rules based on the record field, device type, or other filters, click Add Filter." Also recorded for the deck's staleness sweep: option C is built on Process Builder, which reached end of support on 31 December 2025 - the key is unaffected, but the distractor now names a retired tool.

question: Universal Containers has several large customers that sell their products through dealers. Each customer and dealer has an individual rep who works directly with UC, and each is billed separately. How can an app builder implement these requirements?

The VP of HR wants to allow edit access to Applications to recruiters. How should an app builder configure the proper access?

optionB: Add a sharing rule that grants the users Read/Write access to the Internship records.

optionD: Create a sharing rule that grants the users Read/Write access to the Application records.

question: Universal Containers uses the Asset object to track products that are installed at customer locations. A new object, Asset Inventory, has been created to capture details about the asset. Which approach should the app builder take to show Asset Inventory as a related list on Asset?
optionA: Create a roll-up on Asset. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout.

optionD: Create a master-detail relationship on Asset to Asset Inventory. Add the Asset Inventory related list to the Asset page layout.

question: When an opportunity Close Date is delayed by more than 60 days, the manager and the VP of Sales must approve the change. How can this requirement be met? Choose 2 answers
optionA: Build an approval process that requires unanimous approval from the manager and VP of Sales.
optionB: Create a workflow rule that checks for Close Date less than 60 days and add an email alert.
optionC: Create a record-triggered flow that submits the record for an approval process.
optionD: Build a validation rule that does not allow a user to save the opportunity record.
explanation:
The requirement splits into two jobs, which is why it takes two answers: something has to collect the sign-offs, and something has to notice the change and start the process.
A collects the sign-offs. In an approval step you choose Automatically assign to approver(s), name the manager and the VP of Sales, and then select Require unanimous approval from all selected approvers, which Salesforce defines as approving the record only if everyone approves and rejecting it if any approver rejects.
C starts the process. Submit for Approval is a core action available to a flow, so a record-triggered flow on Opportunity whose entry conditions detect Close Date moving out by more than 60 days can submit the record automatically instead of relying on a rep to remember. Build this in Flow Builder: Salesforce ended support for Process Builder and Workflow Rules on 31 December 2025 and directs all new automation to flows.
B fails on both counts. Its criterion is inverted, it tests Close Date rather than the size of the delay, and an email alert notifies people without recording an approval. D blocks the change outright, which is not what was asked: the delay is allowed, it just needs approval.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_step_approver.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Key A,C stands. The explanation offered Process Builder as an equal alternative to a record-triggered flow, which is now wrong guidance: support for Process Builder ended 31 December 2025 and Salesforce directs new automation to Flow Builder. The unanimous half is settled verbatim by the approval-step article: 'Require unanimous approval from all selected approvers. The record is approved only if everyone approves the request. If any approvers reject the request, the approval request is rejected.' Worth knowing for the rest of the deck's approval items: Salesforce has renamed this feature Classic Approval Processes and now promotes Flow Approval Processes as the modern alternative.

question: DreamHouse Realty is rethinking its sandbox utilization strategy after acquiring Cloud Kicks. The Salesforce CoE already utilizes a partial and a full sandbox, which they refresh on their own regular schedules. Teams are expanding and have to begin each of their small projects in a sandbox before committing to the larger pool for collaborative testing while still keeping costs down. What type of sandbox should each team member use?
optionC: Developer Pro sandbox
explanation:
A Developer sandbox is the right size and, in this org, the right price. Sandbox Licenses and Storage Limits by Type gives it a 1-day refresh interval and 200 MB of data storage, copying metadata only - enough for one person's small project, and refreshable as often as that project needs.
The cost argument is what rules out the nearest rival. Developer sandboxes aren't sold separately; they come bundled with the add-ons the CoE has already bought. The Partial Copy add-on bundles 10 Developer sandboxes and the Full add-on bundles 15, so DreamHouse already owns 25 of them at no extra cost. Developer Pro (C) has to be purchased on top, and its extra 1 GB of storage buys nothing for a metadata-only project.
Full (A) and Partial (D) are the shared pool the question describes teams promoting into, and their 29-day and 5-day refresh intervals make them unsuitable as personal scratch space even if the licences existed to hand one to each team member.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.data_sandbox_environments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should an app builder consider when choosing a template for a new Lightning record page?
optionA: The template cannot be changed after the initial save.
optionB: To view the record page, users need View All Data permissions for the object.
optionC: The page structure will automatically adapt to the device being used to view the record page.
optionD: Select a new template for each type of device users use to view the record page.
explanation:
The consideration that matters is device coverage, because the template you pick is what governs how the page appears across devices, not a separate page per device. Standard record page templates support both desktop and phone, and in Lightning App Builder you use the form factor switcher to preview the page on each device the template supports.
That is what makes D wrong: you don't select a new template per device. And it is why device coverage is worth thinking about up front - home page templates are desktop-only, and record page templates with pinned regions are desktop-only too, so choosing one of those closes off the phone. If a form factor isn't offered when you assign the page, the template doesn't support it.
A is false. You can switch an existing record page to a different template, subject to two documented rules: you can't switch to a template supporting a narrower set of devices, and any component whose form factor the new template doesn't support is dropped at run time. B is false as well; viewing a record page needs access to the record, not View All Data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_page_templates.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.lightning_app_builder_mobile_guidance.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key C stands as the only option that survives, but the explanation overstated it. It said Lightning page templates 'are responsive: their regions reflow for desktop, tablet, and phone form factors automatically', which the documentation contradicts: 'Home page templates are desktop-only. Standard app page templates support both desktop and phone. Standard record page templates support both desktop and phone, except the pinned region templates, which are desktop only. If a form factor isn't on the options list when you try to assign a Lightning page, then the page template doesn't support it.' The defensible version of C is the one the mobile-guidance article states - 'the template you choose controls how it appears across devices' - which is a reason to choose carefully, not a guarantee of automatic adaptation. The rewrite also nails down why A is false, since the same article documents the rules for switching a record page to a different template.

question: An app builder wants to use Process Builder to automate some of the work being done by the sales team. What are three capabilities of Process Builder that can improve productivity? Choose 3 answers
optionC: Send an outbound message.
explanation:
Salesforce's own list of process actions settles this. A process can send an email alert (A), update records including related ones (B), and create a record, which covers creating a child record (E). The full documented set is: create a record, invoke another process, create a Chatter post, use a quick action, work with Quip, launch a flow, send an email, send a custom notification, send a survey invitation, submit a record for approval, update records, and call Apex code.
D and C are absent from that list, and their absence is the point. There is no delete action in Process Builder, and no outbound message action either - outbound messages were a Workflow Rule action, never a Process Builder one.
Build this in Flow Builder rather than Process Builder. Support and updates for Process Builder ended on 31 December 2025; existing processes keep running but bugs are no longer fixed, and Salesforce provides a Migrate to Flow tool. Flow covers every capability listed above and adds the delete that Process Builder never had, through its Delete Records element.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.process_action.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000389396&language=en_US&type=1

corrected.note: Key A,B,E confirmed against the documented action list on Add Actions to Your Process, which contains no delete action and no outbound message action. The explanation was rewritten because it described Process Builder purely in the present tense as the tool to reach for. The same help page now carries the notice: 'Support and updates for Process Builder have ended as of December 31, 2025... For new automations, create flows in Flow Builder.' The key is unaffected - the item is a fair test of what Process Builder could do - but a learner should not leave it planning to build one.

question: Universal Containers uses a private sharing model on Accounts. User A and User B both own Accounts of their own and have both been sent a new account record in an email owned by User C to take a look at. User A is able to open and view the record but User B receives an insufficient privileges error. User A and User B have the same role in the role hierarchy. What are three reasons User A has access but User B is unable to access the record? Choose 3 answers
optionA: User A is on the same account team as User C.
optionB: User A and User B have different profiles.
optionC: User C has manually shared the record with User A.
optionD: User A was granted an additional permission set.
optionE: User A is in a public group that has access via a sharing rule.
explanation:
With a private sharing model, access to one specific account has to come from a record-sharing mechanism, and the three named here are all documented ways to give one user access without giving it to a peer in the same role.
A is account team membership. Salesforce lists the Account Team Member record alongside org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules and manual sharing as one of the methods that determine a user's access to an account.
C is manual sharing, which exists for exactly this case: the owner opens up a single record to a specific coworker, and Salesforce notes this is easier and more secure than a sharing rule when only one record is involved.
E is a criteria- or owner-based sharing rule targeting a public group. If User A is in the group and User B isn't, the rule reaches one and not the other.
B and D are weaker, but not for the reason usually given. Profiles and permission sets can reach record access, through View All Records or Modify All Records, which the documentation says ignore sharing rules and settings. What they can't do is single out one account: they would open every account record in the org, which is a much bigger change than the scenario describes, and neither option states that such a permission is present.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.accountteam_def.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.granting_access_to_records_lex.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.users_profiles_view_all_mod_all.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key A,C,E stands, but the explanation's justification was documented-wrong. It claimed 'Profiles and permission sets control object/system permissions, not record-level access.' Considerations for Using Account Teams lists Profiles first among the access methods that 'determine users' access levels for accounts and related records', and the View All / Modify All article states that those permissions 'ignore sharing rules and settings, allowing administrators to grant access to records associated with a given object across the organization.' So the correct reason to reject B and D is granularity, not category: a permission set can grant account access, but only to every account at once, which doesn't match a scenario about one record.
